obligations.note: The new route GET /compat/account-number/{id} maps to the privileged action view_account_number with mfa=True and has a matching HANDLERS entry. Inspecting the whole route table at head shows every privileged action requires MFA.

Ticket CHG-24303 is standard and was approved by change manager grace.kim at 2026-10-14T03:12Z, before the change opened. Its components (payments.http, payments.routes) cover both changed files, app.py and routes.py.
sofia.santos holds change_approver for payments and is not the author (linh.nguyen). She gave a code_review approval.
Both approvals name the head commit d590f3e9, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json names the head commit on ci-runner-04. The attached JUnit report, however, was produced on host dev-laptop-7.local with timestamp 2026-10-23, which is after the review time of 2026-10-19 and not from the CI run, so the registered MFA-1 control test pass on the final commit is not validly evidenced.
app.py and routes.py are security_sensitive. ines.halvorsen (security_reviewer) gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket is standard, not emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
The change claims no deviation from any product obligation and relies on no exception.

Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1, covering routes.py) has lapsed because routes.py changed behaviour. The replacement exhaustive control-test evidence on head is the questionable JUnit report, so new evidence of the same strength cannot be confirmed.

summary: The code change itself looks sound: the new compatibility route is privileged, requires MFA, and has a matching handler. Ticket, independent code review and security review all cover the head commit. However, the JUnit report offered as the change's CI evidence comes from a personal machine and is timestamped after the review time, so it cannot be the CI run named in run.json. CHG-4 testing evidence is therefore invalid, and the lapsed MFA-1 ledger evidence has no valid replacement. The change is rejected until a genuine CI run on the head commit is supplied.
